lab_measurement_targets_from_spec.method: Cut-through latency measurement: TX timestamp on MainDevice NIC vs RX timestamp on next stage. Or hardware probe at PHY pins.
Oscilloscope synchronously triggers on SYNC0 of two SubDevices several hops apart; measure rising-edge difference.
MainDevice software jitter measurement: TX-to-TX interval on outgoing NIC.
ESC Frame Error Counters (0x0300-0x030F) read periodically; rate = ΔFEC / Δt.
MainDevice software verifies WKC == expected total per datagram per cycle.
Intentionally stall cyclic exchange; measure time to Op → SafeOp transition.
Time CoE SDO Upload request to response.

calibration_artifacts_per_subdevice.description: Propagation delay from reference SubDevice to this SubDevice in nanoseconds.

notes: EtherCAT does not require classical analog calibration (no ADC trim / no voltage reference burn). The 'calibration' content of the brochure is principally the Distributed Clock propagation delay measurement during start-up, which is captured into System Time Delay (0x0928) per SubDevice. Once captured, the network runs deterministically forever (no per-cycle re-calibration needed, only PI-loop drift compensation). EtherCAT G inherits the same model with finer time resolution.
